issues.detail: The Greek 'εκ των πατερων' (from the fathers) refers to the ancestors/forefathers, but the Vietnamese translation 'từ các Cha' can be interpreted as 'from the Fathers' (implying a specific group or divine figures), which slightly shifts the historical/lineal context of the original.

The Greek 'περιτεμνετε ανθρωπον' is an imperative (command) or a general present indicative, but the Vietnamese 'các ngươi cắt bì' lacks the imperative force/urgency often associated with this specific polemic in the context of the surrounding verses.
